Beyond the typical values of the estimated timescales and their ratios, we also examine which timescales correlate the best with $t_\mathrm{dep,\,mol}$.
We estimate this timescale from the mean volume density of molecular clouds under the assumption of spherical symmetry.

We estimate this timescale following a simplified model of shear-induced collision (cite: Tan_2000). The key assumptions are that molecular clouds are randomly distributed in each aperture, and that cloud–cloud collision happens *only* when clouds catch up with other clouds on adjacent circular orbits due to orbital shear.
